title: Drawing a Tile Map
summary: Delve's world is a grid of tiles stored in a flat array (lesson 2.07) and loaded from a plain text file (lesson 10.08), where each character is a tile and special characters mark where the player and monsters start. This lesson writes the level format, the loader with validation, and the renderer that draws the visible part of the map around a camera.
ideas:
- Write a second level with a long corridor and make sure the camera follows the player along it.
- Add a new tile, `~` for water, that is not walkable, and give it a colour.
- Load a tile sheet with SDL_image and draw walls and floors from it.

cards.q: How is the map stored in memory?
cards.a: As one flat vector of tiles in row-major order, with the index of (x, y) being y × width + x.

cards.q: What does the level loader need to check?
cards.a: That all rows are the same width, every character is known, there is exactly one player start, and it should report problems with line numbers.

cards.q: How does a tile sheet make drawing more efficient?
cards.a: All tiles come from one shared texture, so the renderer can batch them instead of switching textures for every tile.
